graph.title: LEGO 40181-1 Bricktober Pizza Place
notes: Page 2 is an intro page (minifigure opening the box, sorting pieces, starting to build). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins are added.

Page 3 steps 1-2: the 1x6 plate is placed across the back short edge of the 6x8 base, then two more 1x6 plates run down the left and right sides, one on each side. Each sits on the base only. They sit beside the first 1x6, not on it, so they don't clutch it.
Page 4 step 3: three yellow 1x4 grooved tiles go side by side inside the frame, on the base. A light bluish gray 1x4 plate goes in front of them, also on the base.
Page 4 step 4: a reddish brown 1x2 plate, a reddish brown 1x1 grooved tile and three light bluish gray 1x1 plates go on the black base in front of the grey 1x4 plate.

The step 4 picture is small and the exact spots of the three gray 1x1 plates are unclear. I took them as sitting directly on the base, so rests_on is b1 for every piece in that step. The grey 1x4 plate, tiles and brown parts sit side by side on the base, so no stacking is recorded between them.
Page 5 step 5: a green 1x3 plate goes on the front-left of the base and a green 1x1 plate on the front-right. Eight light bluish gray 1x1 grooved tiles fill the open studs at the front of the base.
The picture doesn't show clearly which open studs get tiles, so I took the following. Three tiles sit on the gray 1x1 plates from page 4 (b11, b12, b13). The other five sit directly on the base b1.

Page 5 step 6: four red 1x4 plates form a ring around the yellow tiles, on top of the gray frame plates. A red 1x1 plate goes at the front-right corner of that ring. The ring layout is approximated from the small picture. The back plate sits on b2, the left on b3 and the right on b4. The front plate sits on b8. The 1x1 is taken as resting on b4.

Page 6 step 7: two white 1x2 plates stack, then a red 1x2 plate goes on top of them. This stack sits at the back centre of the red ring, and a brown masonry brick sits on each side of it. The stack and bricks are approximated as resting on the back red plate b25. Each brick also touches the plate on its own side: b27 on the left and b26 on the right.

Page 6 step 8: a black Technic pin goes into a side pin-hole of each dark gray Technic 1x2 brick (2x). The bricks sit on the red plates, one at the left of the back and one at the back right. The pin is taken as entering pin-hole.1 on each brick. Neither brick's position is clearly shown, so rests_on is approximate.

Page 7 step 9: two brown masonry bricks go on the red plates at the left and right sides of the yellow area. Three bright green flower plates go at the front right, on the red front plate, the red 1x1 plate and a gray tile. Their exact studs are approximated from the small picture.

Page 7 step 10: the trans-clear 1x1 plate goes on a trans-clear 1x1 brick. A trans-clear slope goes on a second trans-clear brick. I took that pairing from the callout. A third clear brick and one brown 1x1 brick go beside them near the front of the yellow tiles. The clear bricks are taken as resting on the front yellow tile b7. The brown 1x1 brick is taken as sitting on the front red plate b28. These positions are approximate.

Page 8 step 11: two yellow round plates, one more green flower plate and two black round supports go on open studs at the front of the base. The exact studs are approximated, so rests_on is b1 for these.

Page 8 step 12: two silver round plates stack with a silver round tile on top (the callout shows plate on plate, then the finished stack). The stack goes at the front-right, taken as resting on the green 1x1 plate b22. Two orange round tiles go on the green 1x3 plate b23 at the front-left.
I took the lighter silver part in step 12 as the lego-98138 round tile. Earlier pages put some pieces on grooved tiles, which have no studs. That was an over-approximation from the small pictures.
The two silver plates are shown as 6141, matching the parts list. The third 6141 silver plate and the swirled 15470 plate are used later.

Page 9 step 13: a roof layer of two light bluish gray 2x6 plates side by side, one 1x4 plate and one 1x1 plate covers the top of the building. The 2x6 plates rest on the brown bricks, the Technic bricks and the white/red plate stack at the back and sides. The 1x4 plate rests on clear bricks b45 and b47 at the front, and the 1x1 plate on brown brick b48. These supports are approximated from the small picture.
Page 9 step 14: a brown masonry 1x4 brick, three brown masonry 1x2 bricks and a brown 1x1 brick are built up along the back of the roof. All rest on the roof plates b61, b62 and b60.
The 15533 1x4 brick is placed across the back of both 2x6 plates, so it rests on both. The rest of the layout is approximate.

Page 10 step 15: a red 1x1 plate goes on top of two stacked white 1x1 plates, as the callout shows. The finished stack goes on the left front of the roof, taken as resting on b61. A brown masonry 1x4 brick goes beside it on the roof, also taken as resting on b61.

Page 10 step 16: a red 1x2 plate and a red 1x4 plate form a red awning along the front edge of the roof. The 1x2 is taken as resting on b61 and the 1x4 on the 1x4 roof plate b60. Both are approximated from the small picture.

Page 11 step 17: six curved 2x1 bricks make the striped awning along the roof front: green, white, red, white, green and white from left to right. They sit on the red awning plates b72 and b73 and the roof plates behind. Each brick's supports are approximated from the small picture.

Page 11 step 18: two white 1x2 plates stack and a red 1x2 plate goes on top, as the callout shows. The stack goes at the back of the roof between brown masonry bricks. Two more brown 1x2 masonry bricks go on each side of it. All are approximated as resting on the back brown 1x4 brick b67, with the side bricks also on neighbouring bricks.

Page 12 step 19: three stacks, each two white 1x1 plates with a red 1x1 plate on top, are built as the callout shows (3x). They go on the brown brick wall of the roof: one on b83 and one on b84 at the back, and one on b71 at the left. A brown 1x1 brick is also added, shown at the back. It is taken as resting on b66. All these positions are approximated from the small picture.

Page 13 step 20: a red 1x2 plate and two brown masonry 1x2 bricks go on the upper roof area. The supports are approximated from the small picture. The red plate is taken as resting on b65 and b66. One brown brick is taken as resting on b64. The other is taken as resting on b71.

Page 14 step 21: a red 1x2 brick with two side studs goes on the front of the upper level, taken as resting on the red plate b95. A light bluish gray 2x6 plate and a 1x6 plate cap the top of the upper level. The plates are approximated as resting on the brown bricks and the new red brick. Exact supports are approximate from the small picture.

Page 15 step 22: a dark gray grate slope goes on the top plates near the back. A silver round plate with a swirled round plate on top (the callout) goes at the back-right corner of the top. Both are taken as resting on the top 2x6 plate b99. Exact studs are approximate from the small picture.

Page 16 step 23: two white 1x1 plates each get a white grooved 1x1 tile on top (callout, 2x). They go on the top 2x6 plate b99: one at the left near the grate slope and one at the right corner. Two white curved 2x1 bricks go on the front 1x6 plate b98, forming a white awning over the red brick. Exact positions are approximate.
Page 17 step 24: the yellow pizza round tile is attached to the two side studs on the front of the red 1x2 brick b100. It has one anti-stud port, so both side-stud joins use anti.1.1.
A black support goes on an open front stud of the base, taken as resting on b1. A red inverted dish goes on top of it as a parasol, shown in the callout. The support's exact stud is approximate.

Page 18 starts a small delivery vehicle, built separately from the shop. Steps 1-4 build its chassis from a white 1x2 plate, two black clip plates and four black round plates used as wheels. The other parts in the box (slope, red and green 1x1 plates, a white 1x1 plate, the 1x3 tile and three more 1x2 plates) are used on later pages.

In steps 2-3 the clip plates seem to be fixed under the 1x2 plate, with each clip plate's stud going into one anti-stud of the plate. They stick out at both ends and each holds two wheels. The pictures are tiny, so this arrangement is an approximation. I record each wheel as joined to a clip with its stud port, since the wheel has no bar port.
Earlier pages labelled some 1x1 and 1x2 plates as White, but the parts list has too few white ones. Many of those stack plates are probably Trans-Clear. I can't correct earlier entries in this turn.
Page 18 shows the chassis plate as white. I assumed it is the single lego-3023 White plate in the box.
Page 19 builds up the delivery vehicle body. The pictures are small and no callouts show part counts, so the exact pieces and supports below are approximate.

Step 5: two 1x2 plates are taken as added on top of the chassis plate b113, giving a 4-stud body. The picture seems to show a longer body than the 2-stud chassis, so I take the plates as staggered and both resting on b113. I took them as lego-3023 Trans-Clear. The parts list has only three white 1x2 plates, and b113 is the one used.
Step 6: a green, a red and a white 1x1 plate go on the body studs.

Step 7: a trans-clear slope forms the windscreen at the front. A white 1x3 tile forms the roof over the 1x1 plates. A third 1x2 plate from the parts box is not clearly used on this page, so it isn't recorded here.
Slope b125 is taken as resting on b121. Tile b126 is taken as resting on the three 1x1 plates.

Page 20 starts a second small vehicle, built separately from the shop. Steps 1-3 build a chassis like the first vehicle's. They use a trans-clear 1x2 plate, two black clip plates holding four black round plates as wheels, and a reddish brown 1x2 plate on top.

As on page 18, I take the clip plates as fixed under the 1x2 plate, with each clip plate's stud in one anti-stud. Each clip holds two wheels, recorded as joined by the wheel's stud to the clip. The step 1 plate is taken as trans-clear.
The slope, the two brown 1x1 tiles and the second 1x2 plate in the parts box are used on later pages.
Page 21 step 4 shows the last wheel going on the second vehicle. All four wheels were already recorded on page 20, so nothing new is added for it.

Step 5: a second trans-clear 1x2 plate goes on the brown chassis plate b134, with a trans-clear cheese slope at the front as the windscreen. The slope is taken as sitting on b135, though a 1x2 plate has only two studs. Step 6: the two reddish brown 1x1 tiles form the roof, taken as resting on b135. These supports are approximate from the small pictures.
Page 22 shows the finished pizza place with the two small delivery vehicles beside it. There is no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 24 is an advertising page for the Bricktober sets 40180-40183, shown combined into one street. There is no building step, so nothing is added.

The earlier turns put pieces in extra fields (pieces/other_joins) that the graph didn't count. So this reply re-emits every piece as a part and every join as a joined edge, with ids b1-b139. The 139 pieces match the 139 in the parts list. Where an earlier reply gave a different type or colour, this one replaces it.

Corrections against the parts list. b3 and b4 (page 3 step 2) are lego-3710 1x4 plates, not 1x6. They were left out of earlier replies. b2 and b98 are the only two 3666 plates. b44 (page 7) is lego-49668 plate with tooth, not a slope. That leaves exactly two 54200 slopes, b125 and b136.

Colours re-assigned to fit the inventory counts. Trans-Clear 3023: b29, b30, b80, b81, b113, b127, b135. White 3023: b120, b121, b139. Trans-Clear 3024: b43, b88-b93, b104, b105. White 3024: b69, b70, b124. I added b139 as the vehicle 1 plate on top of b113 (page 18 step 3). It had been missed, and vehicle 1 needs four 1x2 plates in total.
Re-seated pieces that earlier sat on studless grooved tiles. The clear 1x1 bricks b45-b47 sit on the 1x4 plate b8 in front of the yellow tiles. The flower b40 sits on the base b1.

Positions on pages 4-21 are approximated from small pictures (see the earlier notes). rests_on is turned into joined edges with ports null, except the pin, clip and pizza joins, which name their ports.
Page 2 (intro), page 22 (finished model) and page 24 (advert) add nothing. Page 23 was not provided. The inventory is fully accounted for by the pieces above, so I assume it adds nothing.

The three separate groups are intended. The booklet builds three independent models: the pizza place (b1-b112, pages 3-17), delivery vehicle 1 (b113-b126 and b139, pages 18-19) and delivery vehicle 2 (b127-b138, pages 20-21). The vehicles are separate toys on their own wheels, and page 22 shows them standing next to the shop. Nothing in the booklet fastens them to the shop or to each other, so I add no connecting edges.
Nothing is added in this reply. All parts and edges from the previous reply stay unchanged.
